category: text-to-speech and speech-to-text API, monthly free credit pool

free_tier.stated: Free plan at USD 0 a month with 20K credits per month plus USD 1 of prepaid voice-agent usage per month. The credits are spent on text-to-speech at 1 credit per character (about 750 to 800 credits per minute of audio, which the plan table puts at about 27 minutes of Sonic-3.6 a month) or on speech-to-text at 3 credits per second of audio (about 1h 51m of Ink-2 a month); the USD 1 of agent usage is about 33 minutes at USD 0.03 a minute, before telephony and language-model usage.
free_tier.notes: models: text-to-speech sonic-3.6 (44 languages; sonic-3.5 and sonic-3 also accepted by the API) and speech-to-text Ink-2; managed voice agents. unverified: whether unused Free credits roll over, because the pricing page describes rollover only in terms of paid plans

interface_detail: REST (POST /tts/bytes and sibling TTS and STT routes) and WebSocket at api.cartesia.ai, versioned by a Cartesia-Version header; Python and JavaScript quickstarts
tooling: raw HTTP and WebSocket with an API key (sk_car_...) from the playground, or the Python and JavaScript quickstarts
chaining: the monthly pool covers the speech-to-text side of a demo better than the text-to-speech side, because 20K credits is about 1h 51m of Ink-2 transcription but only about 27 minutes of Sonic-3.6 speech; run it from a free CI job for small voice-over or transcription batches. Unlike a one-time credit it renews each month.

limits.value: 20K credits per month on the Free plan, shared by text-to-speech and speech-to-text, plus USD 1 per month of prepaid voice-agent usage; with overages off, new requests are blocked once the credits run out
Free plan concurrency: 2 concurrent text-to-speech requests and 8 concurrent speech-to-text requests; on Free plans a request over the limit returns 429 immediately, where paid plans queue it

binding_note: about 27 minutes of Sonic-3.6 speech or about 1h 51m of Ink-2 transcription per month runs out before the concurrency caps matter

identity_cost.detail: the signup form asks for a first name, last name, email address and password, or a GitHub or Google account; the pricing page names no card for the Free plan and the signup form shows none; unverified: whether a phone number, a card or a verification step is asked after the form

reliability_note: a Free-plan request over the concurrency limit fails with 429 instead of queuing
confidence_note: the credit pool, the credit costs, the converted minutes and the concurrency table are quoted from vendor pages; rollover on Free and the card requirement at signup are unverified.
